_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When a target sits inside another target's shadow root, the hiding logic walks into that root and hides content inside the outer target.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.

=== REVIEW FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Target that is a shadow host loses its internal content. `addShadowPath` adds `element.shadowRoot` for every node on the path, including the target itself, so `walk` hides the target's own shadow children. Reproduced by P1: `expect(innerButton).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` → received `aria-hidden="true"`. Light-DOM targets skip their whole subtree via REJECT, so this breaks parity. Fix: do not add the shadow root of a target (or of anything inside a target) to `shadowRoots`.
- [blocking] No test covers the inert path in shadow roots. jsdom has `'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype === false` (reproduced), so `shouldUseInert: true` silently falls back to `aria-hidden`. The "restore everything… shouldUseInert" test passes without ever setting `inert`, so criterion 4's "works with shouldUseInert" is not really tested. Either add a test that stubs `supportsInert` or drop the claim.
- [minor] `shadowRoots` is never pruned, so roots of hosts that were removed stay in the set and keep being observed until cleanup. Not reproduced as a bug; it is a leak-shaped nit.
- [minor] `addShadowPath` only picks up `element.shadowRoot` when the host is already attached at call time. A path host that attaches its shadow root later is not walked. Not reproduced; outside the listed criteria.
